## Summary

Enforces the project's memory model by verifying lazy loading, preventing unnecessary raster materialisation, and reducing memory usage during visualisation. This PR adds regression tests to lock in lazy behaviour, refactors operations to better support adapter-backed array-likes, introduces decimated reads for plotting large rasters, documents memory behaviour throughout the API, and fixes a multi-band statistics bug discovered during the audit.

## Related issues / tasks

- Completes **Memory Model Enforcement**

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking)
- [ ] Breaking change (documented under a "Breaking" heading in CHANGELOG)
- [ ] Docs / tooling / CI only

- [x] `pytest` passes and coverage stays at or above the threshold
- [x] `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass

- Verified that `load_raster()` and the adapter initialisation path remain fully
  lazy and perform no pixel reads until data is explicitly requested.
- Added regression tests to prevent future eager pixel reads during loading and
  to ensure plotting large rasters performs decimated reads within the display
  resolution budget.
- Refactored operations to avoid unnecessary raster materialisation and use
  NumPy public APIs that better support adapter-backed array-like objects.
- Updated raster plotting functions to use `out_shape`-based decimated reads for
  rasterio-backed datasets while preserving exact georeferencing.

  `reproject_raster` transform bug that passed width as height was also fixed.

author: jdx
body:
## Problem

The [release-plz workflow](https://github.com/jdx/mise-action/actions/runs/29794049055/job/88521647762) fails at `npm version 4.2.1 --no-git-tag-version` with `npm error Version not changed` (exit 1).

The chain of events in `scripts/release-plz.sh`:

1. `package.json` (4.2.1) matches the latest release (v4.2.1) → takes the "Nothing to release" branch, then checks for unreleased changes.
2. There are 6 commits since v4.2.1, but they're all `chore(deps)` Renovate commits.
3. `git cliff --bumped-version` returns **v4.2.1** (`WARN > There is nothing to bump`) because those commits don't trigger a semver bump.
4. The existing changelog guard doesn't catch this — `git cliff --bump --unreleased` still emits a non-empty block that isn't *exactly* `<!-- generated by git-cliff -->`.
5. The script proceeds to `npm version 4.2.1` (same version) → npm errors out.

## Fix

Bail out early when the git-cliff bumped version equals the latest tag / current package version, so the job succeeds with nothing to do instead of attempting a no-op version bump.

## Rationale

The Record Treatment link on study.treatment_order passed the order's start date as the scheduledDate URL parameter, so every treatment recorded through it carried the same scheduledDate regardless of which schedule slot was being recorded. The second recording against an order then tripped the duplicate-treatment trigger in study/drug.js ("A treatment has already been entered for this order for this date and time.") while the treatmentSchedule grid still showed the slot as unrecorded, since its status join compares the computed slot time against the stored scheduledDate.

- https://github.com/LabKey/johnsHopkinsEHRModules/pull/667 (same fix for jhu_ehr)

## Cel

Realizacja **P-2.1b** (FAZA 2, slice `Auth/`): przebudowa fundamentu OAuth z P-2.1 pod zrewidowane **D-2.G1/G2/G3** (klucz tokenu = para **środowisko × rola**) oraz egzekwowalny **bezpiecznik D-2.G7**. Środowisko przestaje być wykrywane globalnie i staje się **parametrem** — jedna instalacja rozmawia z produkcją i sandboxem równolegle (lokalnie: odczyt produkcji + zapis do sandboxa).

Punkt celowo oddzielony od P-2.2 (UI + callback) — to zmiana **modelu danych** fundamentu (stałe, klucze opcji, sygnatury), nie budowa UI.

## Zmiany

### `Environment`
- **`detect()` usunięte**, w zamian jawna fabryka **`for_environment(string $environment): self`**. Nic w kodzie nie decyduje już, do którego Allegro idzie żądanie (D-2.G2). Obie instancje (sandbox + produkcja) mogą współistnieć w jednym żądaniu.
- Sekrety czytane **per (środowisko, rola)** wg schematu D-2.G3 `QUTLET_ALLEGRO_{ŚRODOWISKO}_{ROLA}_CLIENT_{ID|SECRET}`. Metody `client_id()`/`client_secret()`/`has_credentials()` przyjmują teraz **rolę**. Nazwy z P-2.1 (`QUTLET_ALLEGRO_CLIENT_ID` itd.) wycofane.
- Jedyne **źródło słownika slotu**: stałe środowisk (`SANDBOX`/`PRODUCTION`) + ról (`ROLE_READ`/`ROLE_WRITE`, przeniesione tu z `TokenStore`). Naturalny kierunek zależności storage → config.

Uwaga: PATCH stanu magazynowego na produkcji NIE podlega bezpiecznikowi (dozwolony, D-2.G7).

### `TokenStore`
- **Cztery sloty** zamiast dwóch; klucze opcji WP `qutlet_allegro_token_{środowisko}_{rola}` (np. `qutlet_allegro_token_production_read`). `save/get/has/delete` przyjmują `(środowisko, rola)`. Stare klucze `qutlet_allegro_token_read/_write` wycofane — migracja niepotrzebna (nigdy nie zapisano).

### `TokenClient`
- Związany z jednym slotem: `__construct(Environment $environment, string $role)` — bo sekrety są per (środowisko, rola). Bez zmian koncepcyjnych poza wyborem właściwej pary sekretów. Komunikat błędu braku sekretów wzbogacony o rolę.

- **PHPStan level 5:** `[OK] No errors`.
- **Smoke czystej logiki** (poza repo, scratchpad — projekt nie ma harnessu testowego): 14/14 PASS — guard D-2.G7 na obu środowiskach (predykat + rzucanie), literały schematu D-2.G3 (`QUTLET_ALLEGRO_PRODUCTION_READ_CLIENT_ID`, `…_SANDBOX_WRITE_CLIENT_SECRET`), derywacja endpointów, walidacje rzucające `InvalidArgumentException`, brak `detect()`.

- `detect()` **usunięte** (plan dopuszczał „znika ALBO degraduje do domyślnego UI") — wybrałem usunięcie: czystszy, nie-spekulacyjny diff, a domyślne środowisko UI to sprawa P-2.2, gdzie ma konsumenta.

body:
## Summary

Two new analyzer rules (21 → 23), plus the previously uncommitted 2.30.67–2.30.74 hardening train.

### AM060 — Unregistered type map at mapping call site (Error)

Turns AutoMapper's most common runtime failure — `AutoMapperMappingException: Missing type map configuration` — into a compile-time error. Semantic `IMapper.Map` (single-generic, two-generic, non-generic `typeof` forms) and `ProjectTo` call sites are checked against the compilation-wide `CreateMap` registry. Reachability honors exact pair, base types, interfaces, `ReverseMap()` directions, and collection element maps.

Fails closed wherever absence is unprovable: no-registration compilations (externally configured projects), open-generic `typeof` registrations, built-in/enum/dictionary/identity pairs, type parameters, error types, `object` sources. Cross-assembly profiles are a documented non-goal.

**Code fix (Scaffold):** inserts the missing `CreateMap<S, D>()` into a `Profile` constructor in the same document, with insertion-point-minimal type names.

### AM061 — Enum member mismatch in mapping (Warning)

AutoMapper maps enums by numeric value, so same-named members with different values (or missing values) silently corrupt mapped data. Every registered mapping direction (forward + `ReverseMap()`-generated) is checked for enum-to-enum property pairs — convention same-name pairs and explicit direct `ForMember(...MapFrom(src => src.Member))` pairs. One diagnostic per misaligned source member on the owning registration.

Honors `Ignore`, member/map-level `ConvertUsing`, non-trivial `MapFrom`, `[Flags]` enums; unwraps nullable enums.

**Code fixes (Scaffold):** name-based `Enum.Parse` conversion, or explicit `Ignore`.

### Also included

The 2.30.67–2.30.74 hardening train that was green locally but not yet committed (AM022 downstream cycle breakers, AM031-family ForPath scaffolds, AM011 honest fixes, AM032 destination-aware null fixes, AM041 deferred ReverseMap, AM001/AM002 ForCtorParam ownership, package compatibility contract).

author: dkoosis
body:
## What

Wrap `query.FindOverlappingSymbols`'s predicate-batch loop in a single read-only transaction (`db.BeginTx(ctx, &sql.TxOptions{ReadOnly: true})`, `defer tx.Rollback()`), and run each batch's query on the tx instead of `db` directly.

## Why

The loop issued its batches as N separate `db.Query` calls, each its own implicit transaction. On a large diff (>250 changed hunks/files, past `overlapBatchPredicates`) the query splits across multiple batches. A concurrent writer — e.g. a reindex in WAL mode — could commit **between** two batches, so the batches straddle a write boundary and could double-count or drop a symbol. Near-theoretical on snipe's static read-only index, but a real snapshot-consistency gap. The tx gives every batch one stable snapshot: modernc.org/sqlite honors `ReadOnly:true` as a plain deferred `BEGIN`, which takes the read snapshot on the first query and holds it until Rollback.

## Behavior preserved

Same predicates, same batching, same dedup, same ordering, same return. All existing `overlap` tests pass unchanged. The only observable change is transactional isolation of the batch loop.

## Scope notes

- `CheckPathStaleness` (runs before the loop, takes `db` not a tx) is deliberately left out of the tx — pulling it in would change its signature and ripple to other callers. Possible follow-up if a fully-consistent staleness+overlap snapshot is ever wanted.
- No concurrency test added: a deterministic mid-loop-writer test isn't feasible without a flaky timing hook. The guarantee is **structural** (verified by construction) and documented in a code comment. Not weakened into a CI-flaky timing test.

`make audit` green (eval repos skipped locally; eval drift reverted).

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
### Why This Change Is Needed

Clinical trial data managers and coordinators frequently interact with massive, multi-section Case Report Forms (CRFs). Previously, typing in any input field dispatched state updates directly to the central store on every keystroke (`onChange`). Because the entire form subscribed to this store, every single keypress forced a full, top-down re-render of the entire CRF structure. On larger forms, this resulted in severe input lag, visual stuttering, and typing buffers that degraded user efficiency and increased data entry error rates.

Our objective was to reduce typing latency to under 16ms (maintaining 60 FPS) and restrict form rendering to only the active input field during typing, while preserving accessibility, keyboard flow, and discrepancy validation.

---

### Key Decisions & Rationale

1. **Local State Buffering (De-coupling Typing from the Global Store)**
   * **Decision:** We transitioned input fields to maintain their own local responsive state during active typing and only dispatch the finalized value to the central store on `onBlur`.
   * **Rationale:** This prevents expensive global state commits and validation calculations from running on every keystroke, keeping input entry instantaneous. It also prevents unfinished, typing-in-progress state from polluting the global discrepancy registry.

2. **Component Modularization & Memoization (`React.memo`)**
   * **Decision:** Refactored the monolithic form layout in `CRFRenderer.jsx` into nested, isolated subcomponents: `FormField`, `FormRow`, and `FormGroup`. Each of these subcomponents is wrapped in `React.memo`.
   * **Rationale:** By dividing the form structurally and utilizing memoization, we ensure React only re-renders components whose props have explicitly changed. During active typing, only the localized `FormField` renders. Upon blur, only the affected field and its parent container re-render to reflect the committed value.

3. **Dynamic Validation & Discrepancy Management on Blur**
   * **Decision:** Discrepancy flag evaluation and visual updates are triggered immediately following the input's `onBlur` event.
   * **Rationale:** This ensures we maintain high data integrity. When a coordinator corrects a flagged field and tabs away, the system evaluates the committed data and updates visual markers/aria-descriptions instantly without polluting the UX during active typing.

4. **Preservation of Accessibility (A11y)**
   * **Decision:** We ensured that standard HTML inputs and native focus management are maintained. Screen reader announcements continue to be broadcasted cleanly via the `useAccessibility` provider upon state changes and row mutations.

---

### Detailed Changes

* **`CRFRenderer.jsx`**:
  * Extracted inline form structures into memoized subcomponents: `FormField`, `FormRow`, and `FormGroup`.
  * Implemented localized text state tracking inside `FormField` using a `value` state hooks pattern.
  * Added `onBlur` event handlers to inputs to trigger `store.setFormData` and kick off the discrepancy evaluation pipeline exactly once per completed input interaction.
  * Preserved hook contexts like `useAccessibility` so screen reader announcements continue to function correctly when fields are updated or rows are dynamically added/removed.

---

### Verification and Success Metrics

* **Input Latency:** Verified that input lag is eliminated (< 16ms) during continuous typing regardless of form size.
* **Render Auditing:** React Profiler confirms that only the active field re-renders on keystrokes. Sibling fields, rows, and groups remain untouched until blur.
* **Integrity & Validation:** Form data submits seamlessly, validation rules trigger correctly on focus loss, and accessibility screen reader announcements are delivered reliably.

## O quê
Fase A da arquitetura de conhecimento — cobre os **5 módulos** cujo **namespace de tela Inertia difere do nome do diretório do módulo**, que ficaram de fora das levas 1/2 (#4621/#4623). Continuação do #4612 + proposal `2026-07-21-taxonomia-arquivos-modulo` → **ADR 0345**.

## A causa (verificada, não é bug do repo)
Nos `Inertia::render(...)` de cada módulo o namespace é **minúsculo/misto**, e é o que o Vite resolve:

| Módulo (dir) | `render(...)` | Pages dir (tracked) |
|---|---|---|
| `Modules/ADS` | `ads/...` | `resources/js/Pages/ads` |

body:
### Context & Rationale

When integrating modern React form widgets into our legacy JSP templates, users relying on assistive technologies and keyboard-only navigation experienced broken workflows. Hardcoded, non-sequential tab indexes fragmented the keyboard focus flow, missing layout landmarks prevented screen readers from indexing the page structure, and inline helper styles isolated key accessibility elements.

To secure adoption in regulated clinical environments, we must comply with global accessibility standards (WCAG). Our goal is to restore the browser's natural focus sequence, enable fast keyboard-only data entry, and ensure real-time validation errors are properly announced.

Because modifying legacy backend Java models or form-generation engines was out of scope, we implemented browser-side focus overrides and updated the global decorator template to unify landmark structures and styles.

---

### Key Changes

#### 1. Dynamic Focus Sequence Cleanup
* **What:** Added a `clearHardcodedTabIndex` function in `main.js` that triggers on `DOMContentLoaded`.
* **Why:** This scans the DOM for interactive elements (`input`, `select`, `textarea`, `button`) with hardcoded `tabindex > 0` and removes them. By handling this entirely in the browser at load time, we restore natural, sequential focus without changing the backend database schemas or layout engines.

#### 2. Page Structure & Landmark Additions (`decorator.jsp`)
* **What:** Integrated core HTML/ARIA landmark roles (`role="banner"`, `role="navigation"`, `role="main"`, and `role="contentinfo"`) within the legacy layout structure.
* **Why:** This allows screen-reader users to easily jump to specific workspaces or skip sidebars and navigation headers.

#### 3. Skip-to-Content Keyboard Link
* **What:** Injected a skip-link immediately inside the `<body>` of `decorator.jsp` targeting the main workspace (`#bodyDiv`). `#bodyDiv` was updated with `tabindex="-1"` to allow programmatic focus.
* **Why:** Allows keyboard-only users to bypass repeating navigation menus and start data entry immediately. The link remains visually hidden until it receives keyboard focus.

#### 4. Accessible Validation Errors in React Widgets (`CRFRenderer`)
* **What:** Updated the React form renderer to conditionally toggle `aria-invalid="true"|"false"` and dynamically bind discrepancy validation messages via the `aria-describedby` attribute.
* **Why:** This forces screen readers to immediately announce specific errors when focus shifts to an invalid input control.

#### 5. Unified Visual-Hide Stylesheet
* **What:** Replaced isolated inline React hiding styles with a single, global `.sr-only` CSS utility class inside `includes/styles_updated.css`. This class was applied to the skip link and form helper descriptions.
* **Why:** Centralizes visual-hiding logic. This layout rule safely hides elements from visible viewports while keeping them fully accessible within screen-reader accessibility trees.

---

### Verification & Build
* Re-built updated assets using Vite (`npm run build`).
* Verified visual consistency across classic forms using visual override tests.
* Validated that keyboard navigation respects natural reading order and that the skip link displays correctly on focus.

### Why these changes are being introduced

Engineers previously lacked immediate, localized feedback regarding code quality and accessibility violations within their editors and local builds. By missing early-stage static analysis, critical compliance defects and syntax bugs were able to bypass early detection, only to be caught during late-stage manual audits or runtime failures. 

To address this, we are integrating build-blocking ESLint validations—specifically focusing on `jsx-a11y` accessibility rules—directly into the Maven build lifecycle across both frontend modules. This establishes a strict quality gate, preventing the packaging of defective assets even when test suites are skipped.

---

### Key Decisions & Rationale

*   **Shifting Linting to the Resource Generation Phase:** 
    We updated `web/pom.xml` to execute `npm run lint` during the `<phase>generate-resources</phase>` stage (matching `modern/pom.xml`). This ensures linting runs and can fail the build prior to compilation, bypassing the risk of developers skipping validations via `-DskipTests`.
*   **Enabling Full `jsx-a11y` Rulesets:**
    We removed the `"jsx-a11y/anchor-is-valid": "off"` override in `web/eslint.config.mjs`. This enforces strict compliance with accessible navigation standards and exposed existing defects that have now been resolved.
*   **Decoupled & Standardized Configurations:**
    Each module maintains its own standardized `eslint.config.mjs` and `package.json` at its root. This allows modern IDEs and local developer tooling to instantly resolve rules, flagging errors inline within seconds of code changes.

---

### Detailed Changes

#### 1. Build Lifecycle & Quality Gates
*   **`web/pom.xml`**: Moved the linting execution step from `<phase>test</phase>` to `<phase>generate-resources</phase>`. The Maven build will now abort immediately with a non-zero exit code if any linter or accessibility violations are detected.

#### 2. Linter Rules & Accessibility Policies
*   **`web/eslint.config.mjs`**: Removed the rule exclusion for `jsx-a11y/anchor-is-valid` to activate comprehensive navigation markup checks.
*   **`modern/eslint.config.mjs`**: Verified native configuration checks and path patterns (`src/**/*.{js,jsx}`) to ensure uniformity.

Adds real accounts to Bogey Book: signup, login, logout, and password reset — and gates the whole app behind authentication (replacing the old "pick a golfer from localStorage" identity).

### Backend
- `POST /auth/signup`, `POST /auth/login`, `GET /auth/me` — stateless HMAC session tokens (stdlib, 30-day TTL).
- Signup creates a **normal** account and sends a welcome email.
- `POST /auth/request-password-reset` + `POST /auth/reset-password` — short-lived (1 hr), **single-purpose** reset tokens, cryptographically distinct from session tokens (a reset token can't be used to log in, and vice-versa).
- `api/email.py` — pluggable email. **Dev mode** logs the message to the console + `dev_emails.log` (gitignored); one hook (`_send_via_provider`) is where a real provider (Resend/SMTP) gets wired later.

### Frontend
- Identity is now **token-based** (`/auth/me`) via a reworked `golfer-context`. A new `Shell` component gates every route — signed-out visitors are redirected to `/login`, signed-in visitors are bounced off the auth pages.
- New pages: **`/login`** (green field, white card), **`/signup`** (with the "you will never receive spam emails" footnote), and **`/reset-password`**.
- Settings → Profile: the password box is replaced by an **"Update password"** link that emails a reset link.
- The header gear is now a **dropdown** (Settings / Log Out).

### Verified
- Signup/login/me, wrong-password 401, duplicate-email 409, no-token 401.
- Full reset flow: request → emailed link → reset → new password works, old rejected.
- Token separation (session vs reset) verified both directions.
- Frontend typecheck clean; pages render.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- **Server-side enforcement**: gating is currently client-side; the data endpoints (`/golfers`, `/rounds`, …) still respond without a token. The token system is built to enable adding an auth dependency to those routers next.
- **Real email delivery**: welcome/reset emails only log locally until a provider is wired.
- The super admin (Tim) was seeded a login directly in the DB so the owner isn't locked out.

body:
Closes #816

## What

`AppBackdrop.vue` is the biggest continuous CPU/GPU cost on the site (Lighthouse ~6.7s main-thread work). This trims its steady-state cost and calms the orb's default drift while fully preserving the cursor-reactive corona (the effect users like).

## Changes

- **Frame cap 30fps -> ~24fps** (`FRAME_INTERVAL_MS = 1000 / 24`). The per-frame easing factors are time constants tied to the frame rate, so they were rescaled by 30/24 to keep the cursor response identical in wall-clock time: pointer trail `0.12 -> 0.15`, `pointerK` in `0.1 -> 0.125`, out `0.02 -> 0.025`. Comments updated.
- **fbm octaves 5 -> 3.** `fbm()` runs per-fragment across the whole screen every frame; 3 octaves keep the corona/aura reading as organic streams with only slightly softer high-frequency detail, which the soft gradients absorb.
- **Calmer ambient drift, re-centered.** The orb-center oscillation amplitudes are roughly halved (x `0.020/0.006 -> 0.010/0.003`, y `0.024/0.006 -> 0.012/0.003`) and the vertical center nudged up (`0.66 -> 0.68`). Drift is kept (not removed) so it stays "never quite still" but mostly holds upper-center. Reading-shield and cursor-flare math untouched.
- **Skip the loop on very small viewports (< 640px).** Below that width the decorative shader isn't worth its continuous fill cost, so the loop stays parked and a single developed frame is drawn (same path as reduced-motion). It's re-evaluated on resize, so rotating a phone into landscape starts it and back stops it; the reduced-motion / visibility / resize logic is preserved via a shared `motionOff()` helper.

## Verification

`cd web && npm run build` (nuxt build) succeeds.

## Summary

`kct net-status` false-reported a pad unconnected on a net that is
electrically continuous through a `through-via → inner-layer segment →
through-via` chain, while `kicad-cli pcb drc --refill-zones` reports 0
unconnected items. The false open blocked ship-ready gating on 4-layer
boards that reach an inner-layer signal segment through a through-via.

**Root cause:** `NetStatusAnalyzer._build_connectivity_graph`'s "Connect
segment chains to vias" block bridged a via only *within a single segment
component*. A cross-layer path
`pad → F.Cu trace → through-via → In2.Cu trace → through-via → F.Cu trace → pad`
splits into three per-layer segment components, and the shared through-vias
never fused them, so the far pad landed in its own island. This is the
pad-to-pad analogue of #4229 (which fixed `pad→trace→via→pour` for the
zone path).

## Changes

- `src/kicad_tools/analysis/net_status.py`:
  - Replaced the per-component "Connect segment chains to vias" block with a
    **per-extended-chain** bridge that reuses the zone-path primitives
    `_merge_chains_via_vias` (union-find over components that share a via)
    and `_segment_touches_via` (recognises trace endpoints landing on the via
    annular ring, not just dead-centre). These helpers were previously wired
    only into the zone/pour path.
  - Added an optional `require_layer_span` flag to `_merge_chains_via_vias`
    (default `False`, so the existing zone caller is byte-for-byte unchanged).
    The pad-to-pad path passes `True` so the via↔segment bond is gated on
    `_via_spans_layer` — a blind/buried via does not fuse an inner-layer
    segment it cannot electrically reach. Through-vias span all layers and
    are unaffected.
  - Applies to **both** default and strict modes. Degrades gracefully when
    shapely is absent (endpoint/centre-proximity fallback; only ring landings
    need geometry).
- `tests/test_analysis_net_status.py`: added `TestThroughViaInnerSegmentConnectivity`
  (through-via + In2.Cu-segment fixtures, no zone).
- `tests/test_connectivity_reachability_4165.py`: added a confirming test that
  the router union-find oracle (`check_net_pad_connectivity`) already reports
  the same topology complete — **no router code change** (secondary ask verified).

## Acceptance Criteria Verification

| Criterion | Status | Verification |
|-----------|--------|--------------|
| Through-via inner-segment net reports `complete`, 0 unconnected (default) | ✅ | `test_default_mode_complete`; fails pre-fix (reproduces `incomplete`) |
| Same in strict mode | ✅ | `test_strict_mode_complete` |
| Blind/buried via must NOT bridge a non-spanned inner segment | ✅ | `test_blind_via_does_not_bridge_unspanned_inner_segment` (stays incomplete via `_via_spans_layer` gate) |
| No new false `complete`; #3914 / #4229 cases unaffected | ✅ | full `test_analysis_net_status.py`, `test_net_status_strict.py`, `test_net_status.py` suites pass (135 tests) |
| Router accounting confirmed unaffected | ✅ | `test_through_via_inner_layer_chain_complete` (router oracle already complete) |

## Test Plan

- New default-mode test **fails before** the source fix (`incomplete`, 1 pad
  unconnected) and **passes after** — confirmed by stashing the source change.
- `uv run pytest tests/test_analysis_net_status.py tests/test_net_status_strict.py tests/test_net_status.py tests/test_connectivity_reachability_4165.py` → 135 passed.
- `uv run ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on all changed files.
- `uv run mypy` clean on `net_status.py` and `router/connectivity.py`.

Closes #4429

body:
The v1.0 coroutine rewrite (#151, 2026-06-18) put the whole P2P **orchestration** — the accept loop, the peer supervisor, and the message **dispatch / serving** — inside the `network` module. But serving messages needs blockchain access (BIP-35 `mempool` → inv, `getdata` for blocks/txs), and only the `node` module depends on both `network` and `blockchain`; the network module cannot (and should not) depend on blockchain.

**Move** `p2p_node`, the message dispatcher / `message_result`, and the `ping`/`pong` handlers to the `node` module (namespace `kth::network` → `kth::node`). The connection-level primitives (`peer_session`, `peer_manager`, `protocols_coro`, `peer_database`) **stay** in `network`, which `p2p_node` uses via `using namespace kth::network`.

This mirrors the **net / net_processing** split in BCHN/Core and lets the node bridge networking to the chain (prerequisite for the BIP-35 `mempool` → inv reply).

Pure relocation, no behavior change. `network` + `node` + `node-exe` + `c-api` build; node tests pass (158 assertions); node-exe runs.

## Summary

- `create_character_tracker()` pre-seeds every `### B{N} Ende` / `Start` / `(geplant)` slot with instructional placeholder prose ("Filled by the harvest tool at end-of-book..."), but `parse_evolution_sections()` extracted that text verbatim with no placeholder-awareness.
- Result: `has_existing_ende = bool(existing_ende)` in `list_series_trackers_for_book()` returned `True` for brand-new, never-harvested trackers, and the `harvest-character-evolution` skill displayed the raw scaffold text as if it were a real prior harvest — misleading on exactly the first-harvest-ever case, and risking "Keep existing" writing the placeholder into the canonical content slot.
- Fix: add a phrase-anchored placeholder-detection regex (`_RE_PLACEHOLDER_HINT`) in `tools/state/loaders/series.py` that strips a slot back to `""` only when it exactly matches one of the scaffold's known hint phrases — not just the bare word "Filled". A code-review pass caught that the initial looser regex would have silently blanked real authored content starting with "Filled" (e.g. `*Filled with quiet resolve...*`); the phrase-anchored version was verified to preserve that case while still stripping all 5 real scaffold variants.
- `raw_body` is left untouched, so the harvest skill's diff display still shows true file content. Detection happens at parse time, so every pre-existing scaffolded tracker on disk is corrected transparently on next read — no migration, no file rewrite.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactor / chore (no functional change)

## Testing performed

- Full suite: `pytest tests/ -q` → **2324 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** (up from 2318 baseline).
- Smoke tests: `pytest tests/smoke/ -q` → **29 passed, 0 failed**.
- Lint: `ruff check` on all 4 changed files → clean.
- Type check: `mypy` — clean (best-effort check).
- Coverage: 91% line coverage on `tools/state/loaders/series.py`; placeholder-stripping code fully covered at both call sites (h3-shape and bullet-shape).
- 4 new/changed tests added across this PR, all passing individually and within their full suite files:
  - `test_ende_placeholder_not_parsed_as_existing_content` / `test_has_existing_ende_false_for_freshly_scaffolded_tracker` — cover the reported bug directly.
  - `test_real_content_starting_with_filled_is_preserved` — boundary/negative test added after code review flagged the false-positive risk of a looser regex.
  - `test_all_placeholder_hint_variants_parse_as_empty` and a new `TestPlaceholderDetectionBoundaries` class (3 tests) — added after test-gap analysis to cover the untested subsequent-band hint variants and lock in the regex's single-line, fully-italic-wrapped boundary design.
  - `test_strips_placeholder_hint_too` — closes a gap found in coverage analysis (bullet-shape stripping branch was reachable but unexercised).
- One integration test deliberately deferred (not added in this PR): a full scaffold → harvest → relist lifecycle test. Both halves are independently well-tested and provably decoupled (writer has zero coupling to the placeholder regex); noted as a good follow-up if the harvest-skill integration suite is ever expanded.

## Deployment notes

None needed. This is a parse-time fix — no schema change, no new dependency, no DB interaction. Every pre-existing scaffolded tracker on disk is corrected automatically the next time it's read (`has_existing_ende` flips `True → False` where it was falsely `True`); nothing on disk is mutated, and the fix is fully idempotent. No CHANGELOG entry included — release tooling owns the CHANGELOG per project convention.

## Related issues

Fixes #394

- [ ] Confirm `_RE_PLACEHOLDER_HINT` in `tools/state/loaders/series.py` matches all 5 real scaffold hint variants (B1 start/ende, subsequent-band start/ende, next-band geplant) and nothing else.

- [ ] Confirm no signature/return-shape changes to `parse_evolution_sections()`, `list_series_trackers_for_book()`, or `create_character_tracker()`.

body:
## Intent

This PR syncs new Kubernetes action bundles from [dd-source PR #26413](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/26413) into the private action runner embedded in the Datadog Agent.

Three sets of changes are synced:

**`pkg/privateactionrunner/bundles/kubernetes/admissionregistration/`** — new bundle, full CRUD for the four `admissionregistration/v1` types: `MutatingWebhookConfiguration`, `ValidatingWebhookConfiguration`, `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy`, and `ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding`. All four are cluster-scoped, so none of the handlers take a namespace input.

**`pkg/privateactionrunner/bundles/kubernetes/networking/`** — new bundle, full CRUD for all five `networking/v1` resources: `Ingress`, `IngressClass`, `IPAddress`, `NetworkPolicy`, and `ServiceCIDR`. `Ingress` and `NetworkPolicy` are namespaced; the remaining three are cluster-scoped.

**`pkg/privateactionrunner/bundles/kubernetes/customresources/`** — extends the existing bundle with seven cluster-scoped custom object actions: `getClusterCustomObject`, `listClusterCustomObject`, `createClusterCustomObject`, `updateClusterCustomObject`, `patchClusterCustomObject`, `deleteClusterCustomObject`, `deleteMultipleClusterCustomObjects`. These use the dynamic client without `.Namespace()`, enabling CRUD on cluster-scoped CRDs.

All files were synced from the corresponding `dd-source` generated handlers with `PAR_SYNC_EXCLUDE` blocks stripped and import paths rewritten (`dd-source/domains/actionplatform/apps/private-runner/src/` → `DataDog/datadog-agent/pkg/privateactionrunner/`). The two new bundles are registered in `bundles/registry.go`.

## Surface changes

No surface changes. New action FQNs are registered in the existing private action runner bundle map and are callable via the same `com.datadoghq.kubernetes.*` namespace used by all other Kubernetes AP actions.

## Automated review results

| Agent | Findings | Fixed | Remaining |
|-------|----------|-------|-----------|
| Go best practices | 4 | 1 (TrimSuffix style) | 3 (pre-existing patterns shared with namespaced handlers) |

## QA guidelines

CI is green. To validate locally, deploy a private action runner connected to a cluster and execute one of the new read actions (e.g. `com.datadoghq.kubernetes.networking.listIngress` or `com.datadoghq.kubernetes.admissionregistration.getMutatingWebhookConfiguration`) via the workflow automation UI.

## What

Migrate `@willbooster/monaco-loader` from **Yarn (Berry)** to **Bun** (isolated linker + shared global store) and restructure tests to the wb convention so `wb test` runs them.

## Package manager
- Remove yarn artifacts; add `bunfig.toml` (isolated + `globalStore`) and `mise.toml` pinning bun (via wbfy); generate `bun.lock`. Runtime deps unchanged.

## Test restructure (wbfy convention)
- Unit tests stay in `test/` → `wb test` runs `vitest run test --exclude test/e2e/**` (9 tests).
- Next.js e2e fixture `e2e/next-app` → `test/e2e/next-app`, Playwright config at repo root (`testDir: test/e2e`). `wb test` runs `playwright test test/e2e/`; Playwright's `webServer` builds the library + fixture and starts it (3 tests).

## Type / build fixes exposed by the migration
- **Global `require`**: stop re-declaring it as `MonacoRequire` (that global's type is owned by `@types/node`/`@types/bun`). Read it opaquely via `getGlobalRequire()` + the existing `isMonacoRequire()` guard; assign it through a cast in tests.
- **Fixture Next build under bun**: `turbopack.root` set to enclose the global-store symlinks; bump `next` to `16.3.0-preview.6` and enable `experimental.useTypeScriptCli` so the build type-checks via the **native TS7 CLI (tsgo)** rather than the classic compiler API (which the native `typescript` package doesn't ship and bun can't patch in, unlike yarn). Root NodeNext `tsc` excludes the fixture app (it has its own bundler tsconfig); the fixture is exempt from `explicit-function-return-type`.

Running the library e2e fixture via `wb test` requires **WillBooster/shared#1053** (library-e2e-via-Playwright-webServer support in `@willbooster/wb`). Until that ships and `@willbooster/wb` is bumped here, CI runs unit tests only. Validated locally against the shared branch: `vitest run test` (9 passed) + `playwright test test/e2e/` (3 passed).

author: rodchristiansen
body:
Root cause of the fleet-wide MSI 1603s since July 20.

The placeholder regex matched bare `$VAR` as well as `${VAR}`. Bare-`$` tokens are ordinary PowerShell variables, and once #30 started filling placeholder keys from the full process environment, pack-time substitution rewrote script variables with build-agent values on any case-insensitive name collision:

- **ReportMate 2026.07.20.2156**: `param([string]$Path)` became the agent's `PATH` value -> ParserError -> exit 1 -> 1603 on every install. 0 of 102 sampled fleet devices picked up the release.
- **CimianAuth 2026.07.21.0350**: `$azureTenantId` replaced with the tenant GUID everywhere, including the left side of its own assignment -> runtime error -> 1603.

Verified against the decoded `CimianPreinstall` payloads of both blob MSIs and the persisted CA logs (`C:\ProgramData\ManagedInstalls\Logs\cimipkg-*-CimianPreinstall.log`).

Fix: braced `${VAR}`-only matching, exactly as the README documents and as `YamlPlaceholderPattern` already does. `${env:X}` forms never match (colon). Adds regression tests for both field corruptions. 220/220 tests pass.

After merge: cut a release and re-run cimian-bootstrap-mgmt so ReportMate/CimianAuth/Cimian are repacked with the fixed cimipkg.

## Dotti's catch
The profile showed **two different review counts** — the hero rating vs the Guest reviews section header (e.g. 4 vs 3).

## Cause
Both paths resolve stop → booking → reservation → review, but dedupe differently:
- **Section list** (`loadContractorReviews`) has a `seen` set → counts each **reservation's review once**.
- **Hero rating** (`getContractorRatings`) pushed a review **per completed stop** → a stay prepped by 2+ completed stops (duplicate booking rows, or the same home across trips) was **double-counted**, inflating `count`, the **average**, and the **5-star streak**.

Verified for Delaney: **28** completed stops span only **25** distinct reservations, of which **3** are reviewed. **3 is correct.**

## Fix
`getContractorRatings` now dedupes by `(contractor, reservation)`, so the count, average, streak, and tier each count a stay's review once — matching the list. Also corrects the operations roster stack-ranking, which reads the same source.

author: jan-kubica
body:
## Why

A differential usability probe drove the generated capability CLI with agents from strong to weak (opus down to haiku). Three sharp failure cliffs turned up where a capable agent muddled through but a weaker one got permanently stuck. Each is fixed here, and each ships with a structural guard so the *class* of bug is caught next time rather than the single instance.

## Fixes

**1. `--input` and value flags now compose instead of colliding.** Previously, passing `--input '<json>'` alongside any value flag hard-errored `--input is exclusive with per-capability value flags`. But a capability body must go through `--input`, so a required flag like `--workspace` (advertised on the usage line) became unusable — the caller had to relocate the value into the JSON under a different key (`--workspace` → `params.workspaceId`), discoverable only by trial-and-error against validation errors. Now the `--input` JSON is the base and each explicit flag overlays its own input path on top (flag wins), so `uploads create --workspace <id> --input '{"body":{...}}'` works. Required-flag enforcement still fires when a flag is unset *and* absent from `--input`.

**2. Discriminated-union validation errors name the field.** A wrong upload body returned one opaque, path-less `body: Expected union value`. It now reports `body.purpose: expected one of "entity_create" | "entity_version" | "agent_skill"` when the discriminator is missing or wrong, and drills into the matched variant's own missing/invalid fields once `purpose` matches.

**3. `auth whoami` verifies a machine key server-side.** For a `STELLA_API_KEY` it previously echoed three static lines and exited 0 without any network call — identical output for a valid or a dead key. It now makes a real authenticated round-trip and reports the server-resolved organization and granted scopes, or fails clearly on a rejected key. The authenticated caller's own org/scopes are echoed on two response headers (returned only to that caller).

## Guards (each proven to fire, then restored)

- **Fix 1:** a codegen invariant test asserts every generated value flag's target path resolves to a real path in its capability's input schema — flag/JSON-key drift fails CI; plus compose + required-still-enforced tests in both executors.
- **Fix 2:** an invariant test that *every* capability-input validation issue carries a non-empty field path, driven by malformed union bodies — a regression to path-less messages fails CI.
- **Fix 3:** a test that the machine-key path makes a real request and reports org+scopes on a valid key, and errors (not a static echo) on a 401.

## Verification

CLI `bun test` 368 pass / 0 fail; scoped API `bun test` (mcp) 88 pass / 0 fail; scoped API typecheck + type-aware lint clean; `oxfmt` applied. No generated catalog/registry/route-map regenerated (changes are runtime arg-handling, error messages, and help text). Fix 1 (compose) and Fix 3's round-trip + rejection were verified live against a dev server with a machine key; Fix 2's message and Fix 3's org/scope reporting are server-side changes covered by unit tests.

author: otenim
body:
## Problem

Two unrelated full-bag scans made `bagwiz walk` feel broken on large sqlite3 bags that carry no `topic_id` index (e.g. rosbag2-written `.db3` files):

1. **Startup**: walk counted the messages of every PointCloud2 topic up front (`compute_topic_counts`) just to keep empty topics out of the overlay picker. Without a `topic_id` index this is a full messages-table scan, so startup stalled regardless of the topic being walked.
2. **Overlay enable**: pressing `p`/`t` in the image preview ran the overlay initialization synchronously on the UI thread — a full TF scan plus, per selected topic, another full scan that read every cloud payload and parsed every point for the colour ranges.

Measured on a 20.6 GB single-file `.db3` (Autoware recording + injected concatenated point clouds, `timestamp_idx` only):

- walk startup → first frame: **12.7 s**, of which 12.4 s was the PointCloud2 count query alone (cold page cache).
- overlay enable: TF walk (~12 s cold) + per-topic full scans + reading and per-point parsing 2.66 GB of clouds, all with the UI frozen.

## Solution

**Startup (commit 1)** — stop counting. The picker lists every PointCloud2 topic; an empty topic now fails the overlay initialization with the existing "has no messages" status (the code already tolerated this via its counting-failure fallback).

**Overlay (commit 2)** — restructure initialization around one combined, non-blocking pass:

- New `walk_overlay_scan`: a single bag pass decodes the TF topics and collects the selected topics' cloud timestamps. Cloud payloads are never materialized — `ReadFilter` gains `payload_topics`, letting the sqlite3 reader skip the overflow pages of rows the caller only needs timestamps from.
- The scan runs on a worker thread; the preview stays fully interactive and reports `loading pcd overlay ... N%` on the status row (new timed `read_key_event(timeout_ms)` in bagwiz_base). Cancellation, re-selection, and worker teardown are handled; a failed re-load leaves the previously enabled overlay untouched.
- The up-front per-point min/max parse is gone: the auto colour range grows from the clouds actually displayed (running min/max), and clouds are matched to frames by bag record time, since header stamps cannot be known without reading payloads.

The remaining cold-cache cost is the single messages-table walk for full TF history, which is the theoretical floor — TF lookups need the complete transform history.

Measured on the same bag:

| phase | before | after (warm) | after (cold) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| walk startup → first frame | 12.7 s | 0.5 s | 0.5 s |
| overlay enable | frozen for tens of seconds | 0.6 s | ~20 s, in background with progress, UI interactive |

After the overlay reports ready, frame navigation, cloud fetch, and TF projection were verified to work without status errors.

## Test plan

- [x] `pixi run -e jazzy-cuda build-core`
- [x] `pixi run -e jazzy-cuda test-core` — 1513 tests, 0 failures
- [x] New tests: `bagwiz_sqlite3_reader_test` (payload_topics skips/keeps payloads), `bagwiz_walk_overlay_scan_test` (combined scan, empty topic, missing TF, cancel)
- [x] Real-bag measurements via a pty harness (cold cache via `posix_fadvise(DONTNEED)`): timings above; progress display; UI responsiveness during load; projection runs after ready
- [x] `docs/commands/walk.md` updated (background load, adaptive auto range, record-time matching)
- [x] pre-commit hooks pass

author: voltagebots
body:
Captures the decision on introducing an LLM judge to make some loops self-autonomous, before any code.

## Decision
A judge MAY close reversible (Type-2) internal loops — test-green iteration, review-cascade convergence, triage confidence — but MUST NEVER be the actor that sends, merges, pushes, or marks ready. It may recommend "ready"; a human flips it.

Four hard constraints:
- Reversible loops only (never opens the outbound gate, ADR-0006)
- Cross-vendor for security-relevant grading (same-family self-grading is theater, ADR-0005)
- Verifier immutability (judge can't write what it grades, ADR-0004)
- Bounded + logged (hard cap stays as backstop; verdicts logged for calibration)

Names the failure modes explicitly: reward hacking, correlated blind spots, verifier capture, ground-truth drift.

## Status
Proposed — promotes to Accepted only after a first judge ships against one concrete loop (candidate: review-cascade convergence) and the four constraints hold in practice.

Updates the ADR index table. Docs only.

author: privatejoel
body:
## What & why

**P2 of the drawing-extraction arc.** A DXF is native CAD — already structured — so, unlike a scanned PDF, it needs **no LLM**. This adds a second source path into the *same* review→commit UI from P1c: drop a `.dxf` and its title block + parts list are parsed **client-side, deterministically**, then committed through the same BOM chain.

**Why client-side + no ezdxf/LibreDWG** (a deviation from the original research note worth flagging): the API runs on **Vercel serverless** — no Python runtime for `ezdxf`, no native `LibreDWG` binary. But DXF is ASCII, so a pure-JS reader **in the browser** is the correct fit, and it's exactly how the XLSX importer already works (SheetJS in-browser). Net: no new dependency, no serverless binaries, no new API endpoint.

## Changes

- **`lib/dxf-assembly.ts`** (NEW, pure + tested) — a dependency-free DXF group-code reader for the subset we need (ENTITIES: `TEXT` / `MTEXT` / `INSERT`+`ATTRIB`) plus a conservative interpreter:
  - **Title block** from `ATTRIB` tags (drawing_no / rev / title / material / scale, heuristic tag matching).
  - **Parts list** from repeated "BOM row" attribute blocks (high-confidence, `method: attribute_blocks`) with a **labelled TEXT-grid fallback** (low-confidence, `method: text_grid`, warned — it only fires when a header row with recognisable column labels exists, so random dimension text never becomes a fake parts list).
  - Excludes BOM-row INSERTs from title-block extraction so a **child `PART_NO` never leaks into the assembly's own `asset_code`**.
  - Emits the **same preview shape** the LLM path produces (asset + lines + warnings + meta), so both paths render + commit identically.
- **`screens/bom-from-drawing.tsx`** — branch by extension: `.dxf` → client parse (no LLM); `.dwg` → steer to "export as DXF" (binary, needs a converter we can't run here); `pdf`/`image` → the existing LLM path. The DXF commit goes straight through **`bom.importBom`** (there's no `run_id`/`extraction_run`) — the same derivation chain `from-drawing` calls server-side. A **"DXF · deterministic"** badge distinguishes it from the AI reader.

## Test

- `lib/dxf-assembly.test.ts` (10) — attribute-block BOM, text-grid fallback, MTEXT formatting-strip, malformed-file survival, phantom-title-row + missing-asset guards ✅
- `screens/bom-from-drawing.test.tsx` (+2, 6 total) — a DXF parses client-side and commits via `importBom` **without ever calling the LLM extractor**; a DWG upload is steered to export-as-DXF ✅
- `npm run check` (tsc + client node --check + cold-import) ✅ · `npm run build` (16.6 kB `bom-from-drawing` chunk emits) ✅ · `npm run verify` (RBAC/RLS/dead-handler/PDF.js audits, 0 findings; new screen not flagged) ✅

## Scope / follow-ups

- **DWG** (binary) is a documented follow-up — it needs an out-of-process converter (LibreDWG `dwg2dxf` / ODA) that can't run in a serverless function; users export DXF from any CAD in the meantime.
- **ACAD_TABLE** cell-geometry parsing isn't attempted (version-dependent + complex); such tables fall to the TEXT-grid path or the PDF/LLM path. The review-before-commit UX makes an imperfect parse safe — nothing auto-commits.
- **P3**: `part_drawing` kind (reserved in migration 184) — the supplier-only child-part detail.
- Built assets (`public/assets/*`) are CI/Vercel-generated and intentionally **not** committed.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
### Why

Currently, during the CDISC ODM clinical XML ingestion process, the `SignatureRequired` attributes on `<StudyEventDef>` and `<FormDef>` elements are ignored. This defaults imported events to have disabled electronic signatures on their associated forms. As a result, clinical coordinators must manually enable these signatures post-import to meet 21 CFR Part 11 compliance guidelines, introducing operational overhead and the risk of oversight.

By dynamically parsing and mapping these standard XML attributes during the ingestion lifecycle, we automate electronic signature enforcement, streamline the clinical workflow, and guarantee compliance with zero manual intervention.

### What

This PR introduces parser-level extraction and database synchronization for the `SignatureRequired` attribute during ODM XML import:

* **XML Parser Ingestion:** Updated the streaming XML parser (StAX/JAXB) to detect and extract the `SignatureRequired` attribute from both `<StudyEventDef>` and `<FormDef>` metadata blocks.
* **Database Property Mapping:** 
  * Resolves corresponding form and event definitions in the database via their parsed OID identifiers.
  * When `SignatureRequired="Yes"`, the system automatically updates the `electronic_signature` flag to `true` on the matched event-to-form records.
  * If the attribute is set to `"No"` or is entirely omitted, the default state of `false` (or the existing configuration) is preserved.
* **Scope & Architectural Guardrails:**
  * **No metadata generation:** This change exclusively modifies properties on existing event-to-form associations; it does not generate new forms or events.
  * **XML Isolation:** This update is strictly applied to the XML/ODM import pipeline and does not impact spreadsheet or Excel template processing engines.
  * **Transactional Safety:** Database updates run within the existing transactional context of the parent clinical data import to prevent partial or inconsistent states.
  * **Unified Ingestion Routes:** The logic is executed seamlessly across both manual UI-based file uploads and REST API ingestion endpoints.

### Acceptance Criteria Covered

- [x] Streamed XML pipeline successfully parses `SignatureRequired` attributes during ODM ingestion.
- [x] Database field `electronic_signature` is dynamically set to `true` for matched associations.
- [x] Automatic signature configurations operate correctly over both UI and REST API channels.
- [x] Omitted or non-"Yes" attributes do not inadvertently override existing signature configurations.

author: bryceewatson
body:
## In plain terms

honestweek decides which project a coding session belongs to by checking whether the folder the session ran in sits inside a folder you listed in your config. A *worktree* is the same git project checked out a second time in a second folder, and people launch sessions from those constantly (one per task). When the second folder lived *inside* the configured one, the folder-path check happened to work. When it sat *next to* it, nothing about the path said "same project", so those sessions fell into the catch-all `other` bucket and the project's session count read lower than the work that produced it.

This asks git instead of guessing from the path: given one folder, git's own bookkeeping says exactly which other folders are the same repository. Sessions are now matched against all of them.

## What you're deciding

Merging changes which project a session gets counted under, and only that. Concretely:

- **Widens:** a session run in any worktree of a configured repo now counts for that repo instead of `other`. If you use worktrees at sibling paths, some projects' session counts go up and `other` goes down.
- **Does not touch:** commit counts, commit verification, handoff reads, repo metrics, redaction, or the fact-fence. Those still read `repos[].path` alone, so a worktree sitting on a feature branch or a detached `HEAD` can never become the basis for a published commit count. Session attribution and commit basis stay deliberately decoupled.
- **Still excluded:** a separate *clone* that merely shares a name prefix (`myrepo-parity`). It has its own git database, so it never appears in the repo's worktree list. The rule is now "is this literally the same git repository", which is stricter than the old "is this path nested inside that path".

Fails soft: unreadable or malformed git metadata degrades to just the configured path. Attribution is a labelling concern and never a reason to abort a build that verification would otherwise pass.

## How it was found

Downstream, in the site that uses honestweek as its `site`-mode engine. Its unattended weekly job is required to run in a dedicated sibling worktree and forbidden from touching the canonical checkout. From there every session for that repo landed in `other`, and the site's own reconciliation gate correctly refused to publish a page showing 0 sessions for the repo beside 5 sessions' worth of items. The job curated a whole week and then could not ship it.

## Verification

- Reproduced from a real sibling worktree, confirmed the abort, confirmed convergence after the fix (the repo's 5 sessions attributed correctly, matching an independent enumeration).
- `node --test`: 371 pass, 0 fail.

## Implementation detail

- `lib/worktrees.mjs` (new): `resolveWorkTrees(root)` reads git's on-disk worktree bookkeeping with Node built-ins only, no shelling out to `git` and no new dependencies. It follows a linked worktree's `.git` pointer file to `<commonDir>/worktrees/<name>`, reads that directory's `commondir` to recover the shared git directory, derives the primary working tree from it, then enumerates every `worktrees/<name>/gitdir`. A bare repository contributes no primary working tree. `attributionRoots()` memoizes the result per configured path (a build is one-shot, so the set cannot meaningfully change under it); `clearWorkTreeCache()` exists for tests.
- `lib/claude-adapter.mjs`: `matchRepo` iterates `attributionRoots(configured)` and keeps the longest *matched root*, so nested-repo precedence still resolves correctly.
- `lib/site/sessions.mjs`: `labelResolver` doc updated; it already delegates to `matchRepo`, so the hero and the digest still share one attribution rule.
- `test/worktrees.test.mjs` (new): 5 tests over real `git worktree add` fixtures — primary/sibling/nested resolve to the same set, a separate clone does not join it, `matchRepo` configured at a sibling worktree still credits the primary checkout, longest-match precedence holds.
- `README.md`: `repos[].path` row now states the attribution/git-read split.

## What this tool does

Adds the **Outreach** sales-engagement provider to AnyCLI as a `service`-type tool (catalog row #66; anycli id `outreach`, provider key `outreach`, lane `oauth_light`, wave 2). It wraps the Outreach API v2 (JSON:API 1.0, `https://api.outreach.io/api/v2`) behind a non-interactive, resource-grouped cobra tree that speaks a provider-neutral flattened JSON shape for agents.

Resources: `prospect`, `account`, `sequence`, `enrollment` (sequenceStates — the core enroll/pause/resume/finish write), `mailbox`, `mailing`, `call`, `task` (list/get/create/complete/snooze), `opportunity`, `user`, `template`, `stage`, `persona`. Auth is a single OAuth 2.0 user access token injected as `OUTREACH_ACCESS_TOKEN`.

## Design summary

- **Type `service`** — no official Outreach CLI exists; implemented against the REST API following the `internal/tools/notion/` precedent (21-of-23 definitions are service type).
- **JSON:API conventions verified against official docs** (`making-requests`, `oauth`, Sequence State reference): media type `application/vnd.api+json` on Content-Type (when a body is present) and Accept; cursor pagination (`page[size]` / `page[after]`, `links.next`); `filter[...]` field filters, relationship filtering `filter[rel][id]` (post-May-2023 form), `filter[q]` global search scoped to Accounts + Prospects only; `count=true` → `meta.count`; action endpoints `POST /{resource}/{id}/actions/{name}` with `actionParams[...]` query params (`tasks/{id}/actions/markComplete?actionParams[completionNote]=…`, `snooze`, `sequenceStates/{id}/actions/{finish|pause|resume}`).
- **Output flattening** — each JSON:API resource is flattened to `{id, type, ...attributes, <rel>_id | <rel>_ids}`; list commands emit `{items, next_cursor, count}`.
- **Error contract** — exit 0/1/2, typed `apiError`/`usageError`, `--json` structured error envelope, JSON:API `errors[]` surfaced verbatim; 401 and 403 `unauthorizedOauthScope` classified as credential rejection; token redacted from error output; 429 surfaces reset headers with no silent retry.
- Full stage-1 research and the five-layer test plan are captured in `DESIGN.md` (a scratch file the batch lead strips at batch-end).

## Review rounds passed

- Independent re-verification of the write surface against official docs on 2026-07-22: corrected task completion to `markComplete` with `actionParams[completionNote]`; confirmed `filter[q]` is officially documented (Accounts + Prospects only); confirmed `snooze` and sequenceState `finish`/`pause`/`resume` actions.
- Code-health review: resource-per-file structure, shared generic `runList`/`runGet`/`runCreate`/`runUpdate`/`runAction` helpers, no god-functions, `gofmt`/`go vet` clean.

## Test status

**Credential-free checks — green:**
- L1: `go test ./...` green across the whole module (per-resource httptest fakes assert method/path/query/JSON:API headers/bearer injection/body shape/flattening/pagination/error envelopes 422·403·429).
- `go vet ./internal/tools/outreach/` clean; `gofmt -l` clean.

**Credential-blocked layers (cannot run without live Outreach credentials):**
- **L2 (real-API harness):** needs a real Outreach OAuth user `access_token` from a registered Outreach dev app + a test Outreach account. Run: `ANYCLI_CRED_ACCESS_TOKEN=<token> anycli outreach -- <resource> <verb>` against live `api.outreach.io/api/v2`. Proves the JSON:API definition field names, env-var injection (`OUTREACH_ACCESS_TOKEN`), and request shapes match the live API. Includes pinning identity JSON pointers and confirming action-name/param casing verbatim.

Regenerated provider projections and the `helio-cli` `replace` build are validated locally per master plan §2 and are **not** committed here (they belong to the Helio-side PR / batch-end merge).

## What changed

- Select the public response source once, based on whether the named `agent_answer` projection exists.
- Preserve intentional empty strings, lists, and dictionaries from `agent_answer` instead of reviving stale top-level mirrors.
- Keep compatibility fallback for legacy agent results that do not contain `agent_answer`.
- Add a router response regression covering every public answer field.

## Why

`_query_response_from_agent_result()` previously used truthy `or` fallback independently for each field. A verifier-approved empty canonical value was therefore treated as missing, allowing an older flat `answer`, citation list, structured result, or calculation trace to reappear in the API response.

The response boundary now has one source of truth: current results use `agent_answer`; only legacy results without that projection use flat fields.

## Impact

This is an API projection compatibility fix. It does not change retrieval, evidence selection, formula execution, answer generation, ingest, Chroma, or embedding behavior.

## Stack

This Draft PR targets `codex/portfolio-core-simplification` and depends on draft PR #79. After #79 is merged, this PR can be retargeted to `main`.

## Validation

- Focused router/projection/import suite: 79 tests passed
- Full unit test discovery: 1,350 tests passed
- `git diff --check`: passed
- No benchmark refresh required for this API-only projection change

author: lfarrand
body:
## What changed

The round-four performance batch: taking the .NET 10 leverage that our codebase doesn''t get automatically. Two commits.

### GFNI-accelerated GF(2⁸) (the marquee item)
Multiplication by a fixed GF(2⁸) coefficient is linear over GF(2), so GFNI''s `GF2P8AFFINEQB` applies it as an 8×8 bit matrix — one instruction per vector, up to 64 bytes wide with AVX-512, independent of the field polynomial (our 0x11D included, even though GFNI''s native multiply is hardwired to 0x11B). `Gf256` precomputes all 256 affine matrices and dispatches across V512/V256/V128; `Fec` gains 64- and 32-lane blocks for both the syndrome scan and the LFSR encoder. The nibble-shuffle V128 path remains the non-GFNI fallback (Icelake+/Zen4+ get GFNI; everything else keeps current performance).

**Measured in-process on Zen 5** (same binary, `DOTNET_EnableGFNI` toggled — reproducible via the new `--gf-probe` mode in the benchmarks project):

| Primitive | shuffle-V128 | GFNI-V512 | Gain |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| RS encode | 0.78 GB/s | 1.28 GB/s | +64% |
| RS syndrome scan | 0.70 GB/s | 1.03 GB/s | +47% |
| GF MulAdd (Cauchy/fountain) | 22.3 GB/s | 62.6 GB/s | **2.8×** |

Honest framing: end-to-end CLI wall clock on this 32-thread machine is dominated by process startup, PNG I/O, and memory bandwidth, so these gains show at the primitive level and on GF-heavy paths (parity/fountain reconstruction, low-core machines), not on the headline 30 MB round trip. Correctness is pinned by an exhaustive equivalence test (every coefficient × every byte value across all block widths and the scalar tail) plus FEC round trips at block-boundary codeword counts — the whole existing suite also runs through the V512 paths on GFNI hardware.

### The rest
- **CRC-32 → System.IO.Hashing**: same IEEE polynomial (check-vector tests pin wire compatibility), carryless-multiply folding (~10× on bulk data). FastPng''s streaming chunk CRC uses a hasher instance; the `Crc` class shrinks to two methods.
- **SIMD Up filter** in both FastPng writer and reader (`Vector<byte>` — no cross-lane dependency).
- **GridSampler interior fast path**: precomputed flat index deltas for non-edge cells (no clamping or per-offset coordinate math), static offset arrays.
- **FrameSignature buffer reuse** (was 1 KB per video frame).
- **DATAS disabled for the CLI only**: A/B on a 100 MB round trip measured ~3–9% slower with DATAS for this burst workload; the library deliberately leaves the embedding host''s GC policy alone.

### Assessed and intentionally not changed
Escape analysis, devirtualization, inlining, code layout, and NativeAOT improvements land automatically on our existing patterns; FrozenDictionary/Regex/JSON items don''t apply. Our concrete-sealed-type injection for codec primitives already sidesteps the interface-dispatch costs that .NET 10''s GDV improvements address.

## Verification

- 401 tests passing (8 new), CLI self-test green, round trips SHA-verified on all measured workloads.
- The GFNI equivalence test self-adapts to whatever tier CI hardware provides; the fallback tier is exactly the previous code.

## Root cause
Windows PowerShell 5.1 `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8` writes a BOM, while PowerShell 7 writes UTF-8 without BOM. The smoke-failure hook therefore changed the installed worker differently across shells and produced divergent failure messages.

## Fix
- Write the temporary smoke-mutated worker with explicit `.NET UTF8Encoding(false)`.
- Assert the exact semantic failure: `Installed worker smoke failed: 0.0.0`.

## Validation
- BOM diagnostic confirmed PS5.1 `EF BB BF` versus PS7 no BOM.
- Smoke harness PS5.1: 10/10 PASS.
- Smoke harness PS7: 10/10 PASS.
- Rollback SHA-256 before/after: byte-for-byte in all 20 harness runs.
- Full deploy recovery PS5.1: 2/2 PASS.
- Full deploy recovery PS7: 2/2 PASS.
- Related v1.5.7 runtime, quoting, prompt, state/event, Codex supervisor and hardening regressions: PASS.
- `git diff --check`: PASS.
- Exactly one test file changed; no production code changed.

## Safety
No deploy, no worker `--once`, no pilot, task remains Disabled, installed config unchanged, canonical untouched. The lossless and executor-neutral worktrees remain unchanged.
